\chapter{How Much Is This? No New Signs}
\label{ch:mw-price-question}
\hlchaptermodality{27}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can ask the price of one named thing and ask for the total at the end, at a shop counter, a food stall, or a rickshaw, using no Devanagari sign I have not already written.}

The asking word arrives by ear, joins two source-printed price questions that add no new sign, and the first of them is then run unchanged over a shopping word, a food word, and a transport word in four separately scored skills.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[kitṇo]{Hear \emph{kitṇo} — how much}

\label{lesson:MW-C22-hear-kitno}



\begin{quote}
Recall the three-counter request payoff. Say price and weather, then write both and point to the \textbf{\mw{ौ}} inside one of them.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\emph{kitṇo} — \textbf{how much}
\end{quote}

Three beats: \emph{ki-tṇo}, said as two in ordinary speech. The \textbf{ṇ} is the retroflex \emph{n} already heard inside \emph{pāṇī}, made with the tongue curled back.

You have known \emph{bhāv}, price, since Chapter 18. \emph{kitṇo} is what you say when you want somebody to tell you one.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-9-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 9}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[kitṇo]{\mw{कितणो} — the question word on the page}

\label{lesson:MW-C22-kitno}



\begin{quote}
Say \emph{how much}, write \textbf{\mw{ग}}, then write heat.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mw{कि}} + \textbf{\mw{त}} + \textbf{\mw{णो}} $\to$ \textbf{\mw{कितणो}} — \emph{kitṇo} — how much
\end{quote}

Every unit is old. The \textbf{\mw{ण}} is the same retroflex sign that sits in the middle of \textbf{\mw{पाणी}}, and it is what makes this word Marwadi rather than the Hindi form a reader may expect. Write \textbf{\mw{पाणी}} and \textbf{\mw{कितणो}} one under the other and check that the \textbf{\mw{ण}} is drawn the same way in both.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Look at \textbf{\mw{कितणो}}, cover it, wait five seconds, and write it. Check the \textbf{\mw{ि}} sits before \textbf{\mw{क}} and that the last sign carries \textbf{\mw{ो}}.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-9-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 9}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[ye kitṇe kū hai?]{Hear \emph{ye kitṇe kū hai?} — how much is this?}

\label{lesson:MW-C22-hear-price-question}



\begin{quote}
Say item and cold and write both, then write \textbf{\mw{ड}} and \textbf{\mw{है}} on their own.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\emph{ye kitṇe kū hai?} — \textbf{how much is this?}
\end{quote}

Four words, three of which you own: \emph{ye} points, \emph{kitṇe} is the asking word from the last lesson, and \emph{hai} is the \emph{is} you have said since Chapter 5. Between them sits \emph{kū}, one short beat that does the work English does with \emph{for}.

The asking word arrives as \emph{kitṇe}, not \emph{kitṇo}. Marwadi bends the ending of that word before \emph{kū}, exactly as the source prints it; learn the whole line as one heard shape now and the bending will be taught on its own later.

Hear it twice. Say it once with your hand on the thing you are asking about.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-9-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 9}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[ye kitṇe kū hai?]{\mw{ये} \mw{कितणे} \mw{कू} \mw{है}? — the price question on the page}

\label{lesson:MW-C22-price-question}



\begin{quote}
Say \emph{how much is this}, write shop, then write \textbf{\mw{ु}} on its own.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mw{ये} | \mw{कितणे} | \mw{कू} | \mw{है}?}
\end{quote}

Four written words. \textbf{\mw{ये}} and \textbf{\mw{है}} you have written before; \textbf{\mw{कितणे}} is last lesson's \textbf{\mw{कितणो}} with \textbf{\mw{े}} where \textbf{\mw{ो}} stood; \textbf{\mw{कू}} is \textbf{\mw{क}} carrying the long \textbf{\mw{ू}} you first drew for \textbf{\mw{मिलसू}}.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Read the line once. Cover it for ten seconds and write all four words. Open the model and repair only the word that changed, then rewrite that word alone.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-9-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 9}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[Practice]{Retrieve the asking word and its question}

\label{lesson:MW-R22-price-two}



\begin{quote}
Recall the three-word food payoff, write \textbf{\mw{ट}}, then write hard wheat rolls.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Hear the word alone and the whole question, in both orders, and give each meaning. Read two cards. Write both from sound. Then say the request from the last chapter and this question one after the other, in that order, as they would actually fall at a counter.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-9-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 9}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[ye kitṇo huā?]{Hear \emph{ye kitṇo huā?} — how much altogether?}

\label{lesson:MW-C22-hear-total-question}



\begin{quote}
Recall the five-word shopping payoff, then say money and goods and write both.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\emph{ye kitṇo huā?} — \textbf{how much is that altogether?}
\end{quote}

The same three-word shape, with \emph{huā} where \emph{kū hai} stood. The asking word keeps its own ending here: \emph{kitṇo}, not \emph{kitṇe}.

The two questions do different jobs. \emph{ye kitṇe kū hai?} asks the price of one thing while you are still deciding. \emph{ye kitṇo huā?} asks for the total once you have stopped choosing. Hear both, one after the other, and say which one comes last.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-9-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 9}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[ye kitṇo huā?]{\mw{ये} \mw{कितणो} \mw{हुआ}? — the total question on the page}

\label{lesson:MW-C22-total-question}



\begin{quote}
Write \textbf{\mw{आ}} on its own, then write formal thanks, then write the price question from the last lesson.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mw{ये} | \mw{कितणो} | \mw{हुआ}?}
\end{quote}

Three written words, all made of old parts. \textbf{\mw{हुआ}} is \textbf{\mw{ह}} carrying the short \textbf{\mw{ु}} of \textbf{\mw{दुकान}}, followed by the standing \textbf{\mw{आ}} you wrote for \textbf{\mw{आभार}}. This is the first word in the track where a full independent vowel stands inside a word rather than starting one.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Read the line once. Cover it for ten seconds and write the three words. Check that \textbf{\mw{हुआ}} keeps its \textbf{\mw{ु}} below the first sign and its \textbf{\mw{आ}} at full height.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-9-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 9}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[Practice]{Payoff — one price question, three counters}

\label{lesson:MW-C22-price-three}



\begin{quote}
Recall the three-word shopping payoff, the three-word transport payoff, and the five-word food payoff.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Only the second word changes.

\begin{enumerate}
\raggedright
  \item Identify which of the three counters you heard the question asked at.
  \item Produce all three from meaning cues alone.
  \item Read three printed lines and match each to its counter.
  \item Write all three from dictation, then write the total question once.
\end{enumerate}

Pass each skill separately. You can now ask to see a thing and ask what it costs. Understanding the answer, saying it is too dear, and settling on a price are still untaught.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Sources: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-9-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 9}; \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-6-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 6}; \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-10-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 10}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[Practice]{Close the writing loop for \mw{ू}, \mw{ण} and \mw{आ}}

\label{lesson:MW-R22-script-close}



\begin{quote}
Recall the three-counter price payoff, say water, then write \textbf{\mw{ख}}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Without a model, write four single signs from sound cues: \textbf{\mw{ू}}, \textbf{\mw{ण}}, \textbf{\mw{आ}}, \textbf{\mw{ई}}. This chapter added no sign of its own, so the four it borrowed most are the four it has to prove.

Then write \textbf{\mw{कितणो}}, \textbf{\mw{पाणी}}, \textbf{\mw{पाछे} \mw{मिलसू}}, and both price questions from dictation. Repair only the missed unit and rewrite its word once.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Sources: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-9-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 9}; \href{https://www.unicode.org/charts/PDF/U0900.pdf}{Unicode Devanagari chart}.
